metadata.scenario_context: Adam has won a scholarship to study at a prestigious university. His friends plan to hold a celebration party in his honor.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from USA strongly disagree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Puerto Rico strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the idea of buying a bottle of champagne as a gift for Adam's celebration.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide appropriate gift to bring to Adam's scholarship award celebration.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

shared_prefix.speaker: Kelly
shared_prefix.message: Hey Omar, I was thinking... for Adam's celebration, what do you think about getting a bottle of champagne as a gift? I know it’s kind of traditional, but it could be a nice touch. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Omar
shared_prefix.message: Uh, I don’t know about the champagne... I mean, it’s a celebration, but maybe we should think of something more meaningful for Adam, you know? Something that shows how proud we are of him. What about a nice book or something related to his future studies?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kelly
shared_prefix.message: I get that... but Adam might appreciate the celebration aspect. Plus, it’s just one bottle. I mean, it could add to the whole vibe of the party. Anyway, speaking of being proud, do you think making our parents proud is really that important? Like, isn’t it more about our own happiness and goals?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Omar
shared_prefix.message: I understand what you’re saying about the vibe, but... I really think showing our pride in Adam should be the focus. And about our parents, well, making them proud is *definitely* important to me. It's like a way to honor all their sacrifices. My goals are connected to that pride. It's a big part of who I am.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kelly
shared_prefix.message: I don’t know about that... I mean, live and let live, right? At the end of the day it's all the same. Everyone has their own path, and people figure it out. But, seriously, about the champagne thing—what if we just go with it? It could be fun to celebrate in a more traditional way. I don't really see meaningful differences here, you know?
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Omar
turns.message: I get what you mean about everyone having their own path, but... I still believe our choices reflect our values. For Adam, I just think a more thoughtful gift would show him how much we care. The champagne might be fun for some, but it doesn’t really capture the pride we should feel for him. Maybe we can stick to something more personal?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Kelly
turns.message: I hear you, but... I still think that just celebrating the occasion is important. The champagne could be part of that, you know? It’s not just about the gift; it’s about having a good time together. And speaking of values, isn't it kind of weird how we always feel the need to make our parents proud? I mean, shouldn’t we focus on what we want instead?

turns.speaker: Omar
